assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Current
items.clue: Rate of flow of charge through a cross-section.

items.label: Coulomb
items.clue: Unit: the amount passing a place in a wire when 1 A flows for 1 s.

items.label: Capacitance
items.clue: Quantity for parallel plates that is proportional to area A and to 1/d.

items.label: Series
items.clue: Arrangement in which every capacitor holds the same charge Q; total C below the smallest.

questions.stem: Several wires meet at a junction in a circuit with steady currents. A student measures a current of 1.20 A in one wire leading into the junction, and currents of 0.70 A and 0.40 A in two wires leading out of it. The ammeters are ideal and read correctly. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The other wires at the junction carry a net current of 0.10 A away from it.
0.10 A of the current was used up as charge passed through the junction.
Charge is building up at the junction at a rate of 0.10 C each second.
An unmeasured wire must carry 2.30 A, the sum of the three measured currents.

questions.stem: Predict first. An uncharged parallel-plate capacitor is connected to a battery and left until it is fully charged. Which statement correctly describes how the capacitor becomes charged?

options.text: Electrons move from one plate, through the wires and battery, to the other plate.
Electrons cross the gap between the two plates, from one plate to the other.
The battery creates new charge and places some on each of the two plates.
The battery adds charge to one plate, and the other plate remains neutral.

questions.stem: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has a capacitance of 16 pF. A second air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has plates with three times the area of the first capacitor's plates, and its plates are twice as far apart. What is the capacitance of the second capacitor?

Four identical capacitors, each of capacitance C, are first connected all in parallel, giving an equivalent capacitance C_X. They are then reconnected all in series, giving an equivalent capacitance C_Y. How does C_X compare with C_Y?

options.text: C_X is the same as C_Y.

questions.stem: A coaxial cylindrical capacitor of length L consists of a metal cylinder of radius a inside a thin metal cylindrical shell of radius b, with vacuum between them; L is much greater than b. Using Gauss's law, which expression gives the capacitance?

In an electron beam in a vacuum tube, 1.5 × 10¹⁵ electrons pass through a cross-section of the beam in 8.0 s at a steady rate. What is the magnitude of the current in the beam? Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
A parallel-plate capacitor is connected to an ideal 12 V battery. When the capacitor is fully charged, its positive plate carries a charge of 3.6 × 10⁻⁵ C. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?

An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the supply. Its plates are then pulled apart to twice their separation. What happens to the charge on each plate, the potential difference across the capacitor and the energy it stores?

options.text: Charge unchanged; potential difference doubles; energy doubles.
Charge halves; potential difference unchanged; energy halves.
Charge unchanged; potential difference halves; energy halves.
Charge, potential difference and energy are all unchanged.

questions.explanation: Disconnected, the charge has nowhere to go: Q is fixed. C ∝ 1/d halves, so the potential difference Q/C doubles and the energy ½Q²/C doubles. The extra energy is the work done pulling the attracting plates apart.

questions.stem: One plate of a parallel-plate capacitor carries a charge of +6.0 μC and the other carries −6.0 μC. The positive plate is at an electric potential of +2.5 V and the negative plate is at −1.5 V. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
A copper wire carries a current directed toward the right. Which statement describes the motion of the charge carriers that make up this current?

options.text: Positive ions drift toward the right, while the free electrons stay in their places.
Free electrons drift toward the left, while the positive ions drift toward the right.
Free electrons drift toward the left, while the positive ions stay in their places.
Free electrons drift toward the right, the same direction as the conventional current.

questions.stem: A capacitor consists of a metal sphere of radius 2.0 cm inside a thin, concentric metal shell of radius 3.0 cm, with air between them. The sphere carries charge +Q and the shell carries −Q. What is the capacitance? Use k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C².

A wire consists of two sections made of the same metal and joined end to end. The diameter of section 2 is half the diameter of section 1. The wire carries a steady current, which is the same in both sections. What is the ratio v₂/v₁ of the drift speed of the free electrons in section 2 to that in section 1?
